chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu'l-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Uthman al-Ahwal narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Mihran narrated to us. He said: I visited al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and with him was a delegation of the Shia. So I heard him say:
O community of the Shia! Be an adornment for us, and do not be a disgrace for us. Speak beautifully to the people. Guard your tongues and restrain them from superfluous and ugly speech.

key_terms.الفضول: Superfluous speech, idle talk, unnecessary words
key_terms.زينًا: Adornment, ornament, honor — to be a source of pride
key_terms.شينًا: Disgrace, shame, blemish — the antonym of زين
key_terms.معاشر: O community of / O gathering of — a vocative address to a collective

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about being an adornment for Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addressed a gathering of his Shia followers through Sulayman ibn Mihran (al-A'mash), exhorting them to be a source of pride and honor for the Imams through exemplary conduct, kind speech toward all people, and strict restraint of the tongue from idle talk and offensive words. This teaching reflects the Imam's concern that the Shia community's behavior directly reflects upon the reputation of Ahl al-Bayt in the wider Muslim society.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Ahmad b. Hashim al-Mu’addab (ra) narrated to us. He said: Abu’l `Abbas Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. `Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim b. Bahlul narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. `Uthman al-Ahwal narrated to us. He said: Sulayman b. Mehran narrated to us. He said: I visited al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as), and with him was a delegation of Shi`a. So, I heard him say:
O Shi`a! Be an adornment for us, and do not be a disgrace for us. Speak beautifully to the people. Guard your tongues and stop them from superfluous and ugly sayings.
